safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.66 days

narrative: Material PL3__M3EC695C shows moderate daily demand variability (CV=32.5%) with highly volatile lead times (CV=80%), making a buffer stock essential. The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock and orders at MOQ=1774 very frequently (~120 orders/year), driving excessive ordering costs. An (r,Q) policy with SS=1409 and Q=20788 achieves 95% service level, cuts total annual costs by 89%, and respects the 22,197-unit storage cap. The EOQ of 40,568 is halved by the capacity constraint — storage expansion would unlock further savings.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binds: EOQ 40568 capped to 20788 (max_storage_units - safety_stock = 20788)

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Fixed Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is moderately variable but continuous (non-intermittent, 76% non-zero days) and lead times are volatile, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal: the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty while the fixed Q exploits EOQ economics.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity caps Q at 20,788 (vs EOQ 40,568), increasing annual ordering cost vs unconstrained optimum. If storage is expanded above 21,356 units, the full EOQ becomes feasible and saves an additional ~$383/year in ordering costs.
